subject: Egress firewall review + HSM key rotation plan for CopperLane private deployment
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@copperlane.com>, Sally Jones <sally.jones@copperlane.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Egress firewall review + HSM key rotation plan for CopperLane private deployment

Hi Alex / Sally —

Congrats on finalizing the SOW. Before our Private deployment cutover we want to align on two tightly-coupled items that often cause last-minute delays: 1) egress firewall rules for private endpoints and agent telemetry, and 2) HSM key rotation/bring-your-own-key expectations for the on-prem package.

High-level asks from our side:
- Share an egress IP allowlist and any proxy/inspection appliances that will sit between our appliance and the internet.
- Confirm whether CopperLane will manage the HSM (YubiHSM / AWS CloudHSM) or if Redwood should generate and escrow keys for the on-prem agents.
- Walk through the proposed maintenance window for key rotation and whether staggered rotation is acceptable for availability.

I've attached a draft network diagram and a CSV template for egress IPs. Aditya and Grace are copied to own the runbook during implementation. Can we schedule a 45-minute technical prep call this week (Tue/Wed preferred)? If you send preferred times I'll lock it.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0112

Attachments: copperlane-network-diagram-v2.png, egress-ip-list.csv
From: Alex Martin <alex.martin@copperlane.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sally Jones <sally.jones@copperlane.com>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Egress firewall review + HSM key rotation plan for CopperLane private deployment

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers:
- We'll attach the egress IPs and NAT gateway ranges by EOD (they're maintained in our infra repo).
- CopperLane will be using AWS CloudHSM in the customer VPC. We propose Redwood integrates with our CloudHSM instances via the internal endpoint (no internet egress for keys).
- For rotation windows: we typically prefer a single maintenance window per month, but we can consider a staggered approach if Redwood requires zero-downtime rotations.

Also looping Ops alias — they will give the CIDR ranges. 

Alex Martin
Infra Lead, CopperLane Systems
alex.martin@copperlane.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@copperlane.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sally Jones <sally.jones@copperlane.com>

Date: Tue, 28 May 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Egress firewall review + HSM key rotation plan for CopperLane private deployment

Alex / Sally —

Thanks. A few technical notes from the implementation team ahead of the call:
- Redwood's on-prem agent makes outbound TLS connections to our Private Control Plane over 443. The control-plane FQDNs are on the diagram; if your inspection appliance performs TLS interception, we need a list of certificates to pin or a bypass for those FQDNs.
- For CloudHSM: we can integrate with your internal CloudHSM endpoint using mTLS and the CloudHSM client. We'll need a short-lived cert for the initial bootstrap; would you prefer us to generate a CSR and have CopperLane sign it?
- Egress ports: 443 outbound (control), 5222 optional for agent signaling fallback, 53 for DNS. We avoid persistent inbound ports to the appliance.
- Key rotation plan: we support rolling key rotation per-agent. If you want single-window rotation across agents, expect a brief cache-miss on startup (KV cache warmup) per agent — typical impact 5–15s per instance.

I've penciled in Wed 28 May 11:30–12:15 PT for a technical prep. If that works I'll send calendar invites and include a brief agenda (network mapping, HSM integration steps, rollback plan).

—Aditya
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Attachment: hsm-key-rotation-runbook.pdf (draft)
From: Sally Jones <sally.jones@copperlane.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Alex Martin <alex.martin@copperlane.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Egress firewall review + HSM key rotation plan for CopperLane private deployment

Thanks team — Wed 11:30 PT works for us. A few additional constraints from security:
- No agent should have a long-lived key material on disk. All keys must be in volatile memory and retrieved from CloudHSM during bootstrap where possible.
- We require proof of concept of rotation (logs + audit trail) before we sign the final runbook. Can Redwood provide a short demo or recording showing a rotation with audit logs?
- For egress, we will provide a NAT range and will require that Redwood's control-plane outbound IPs are allowed only to that NAT range (least privilege).

Sally Jones
Security Manager, CopperLane Systems

Alex / Sally —

Great call yesterday — thanks for the clear requirements. Quick summary and next steps (action owners in parens):
1) CopperLane to deliver final NAT ranges and CA bundle for any TLS interception (Alex / Ops) — due Mon 05 Jun 2028.
2) Redwood to share a recorded demo and a sanitized audit log showing a rolling HSM rotation (Aditya) — planned deliverable Tue 06 Jun 2028.
3) Update runbook with staggered-rotation option and a fallback to single-node rotation if start-up cache warmup exceeds 30s (Grace) — draft update by Thu 08 Jun 2028.
4) Technical dry run (non-prod) scheduled for Tue 13 Jun 2028; detailed checklist and test cases will be shared one week prior. (All)

Attachments included: updated network diagram with tentative proxy bypasses and the draft runbook. Please reply with any corrections to the action items. Once we have the NAT ranges and the demo, we will request the production cutover window.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
